content.title: About
content.content: Anisette toast is a crunchy biscuit coated with a sweet anisette‑and‑pineapple glaze. It is made from whole‑grain bread that is toasted to a golden crisp, then drizzled with a fragrant glaze that gives it a distinctive sweet‑spicy flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first anisette toast appeared in 1998 as part of a sweet snack line.
The glaze contains natural anise extract, giving it a subtle licorice aroma.
Toast pieces are often used as garnish for desserts and cocktails.
In some countries they are served with hot milk as a sweet breakfast treat.
The biscuits stay crunchy thanks to a double‑bake process: first the bread, then the glazed piece.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain bread provides dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Anise extract contains anethole, a compound with antioxidant properties.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many sweets, anisette toast contains a modest amount of fat.

items.title: Provides vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and supports the nervous system.

items.title: Moderate sugar level
items.content: The glaze is sweet but its amount is controlled, making the product more balanced.

items.title: Anise allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to anise.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Despite moderation, the product still contains sugar and is not suitable for uncontrolled diabetes.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The crunchy biscuit is relatively calorie‑dense, so portion control is recommended.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Made from wheat bread, it is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Anisette toast can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, added to yogurt, ice cream, or used as a decorative element in desserts. It pairs well with hot tea, coffee, or milk.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the toasts in an airtight package in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life keep them in the refrigerator to maintain crunch and prevent moisture absorption.
